data.name: Juhaym
data.gender_notes: Juhaym is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who was born from the sea. In history, Juhaym was a chief of the Arab tribe of Ghassan who resisted the Byzantine invasions of the Levant. The name Juhaym carries the meaning “Sea-born, born from the sea” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Juhaym usually hope their child will grow to embody sea-born, born from the sea and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and resilience, as well as a deep connection to nature and the elemental forces.
data.etymology: Juhaym belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sea-born, born from the sea.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Juhaym total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Juhaym carries a rich cultural significance as it was historically possessed by a prominent figure, the chief of the Arab tribe of Ghassan, Juhaym ibn Sabah. He displayed exceptional bravery and resistance against Byzantine invasions of the Levant during the early 6th century. Juhaym's name became synonymous with courage and resistance against foreign aggression, inspiring generations of Arab poets and historians.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Juhaym can evoke the sense of being a protector or guardian. The Arabic root "h-w-m" in the name is associated with the concept of protection and defense. In a broader spiritual context, Juhaym can be seen as a symbol of resilience and determination against the challenges of life, just as the historical figure demonstrated in resisting the Byzantine invasions. This name can also serve as a reminder to always stand firm against adversity and strive for the protection and preservation of one's values and beliefs.

historical_references.context: Juhaym ibn Safwan, a prominent Qadari scholar who denied the divine predestination, was born in Kufa. He was known for his opposition to the Ash'ari school of thought which upheld the belief in God's predestination. Juhaym's teachings were influential during the 6th/12th century and led to the emergence of the Juhaymiyah sect.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Dhahabi's Mizan al-Ittidal The name Juhaym carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Juhaym ibn Zararah, a scholar from Damascus, was a significant figure in the intellectual debates of the 7th/13th century. He was a student of the renowned jurist and theologian, Ibn Taymiyyah, and is known for his criticisms of the unorthodox beliefs of some Sufis and philosophers. Juhaym's works were influential in refuting certain unorthodox trends in Islamic thought during this period.
